name: Data, AI & Analytics
short: Dashboards, data warehouses, custom AI agents, document AI, and forecasting that turn your data into decisions and your busywork into automation.
intro: Most businesses already collect the data they need to make better decisions; it is just trapped in separate tools. These solutions bring it together, put it in front of the right people, and apply AI where it saves real time, with guardrails that keep people in control.

solutions.name: Business Intelligence & Reporting Dashboards
solutions.tagline: Live dashboards built from every system, instead of a monthly spreadsheet someone rebuilds by hand.
solutions.text: A centralized reporting and business intelligence platform that pulls data from your CRM, ERP, POS, marketing tools, and financial systems into live dashboards instead of a monthly spreadsheet someone has to manually rebuild. Custom dashboards are built around the metrics that actually matter to your business (revenue, margin, customer acquisition cost, pipeline velocity, whatever leadership needs to see) with drill-down detail available on demand. Automated report delivery pushes key numbers to stakeholders' inboxes on a schedule, and role-based access means every team sees the data relevant to them without wading through everyone else's.
for: Leadership teams making decisions on stale numbers
Operations managers tracking KPIs across locations
Finance teams rebuilding the same reports monthly
features: CRM, ERP, POS, ads, and accounting data combined.
Agreed formulas so everyone uses the same numbers.
Filter, drill down, and compare periods.
Reports emailed or posted to Slack automatically.
Notifications when a metric moves outside its range.
Each team sees the data relevant to them.
problems: Reports take days to compile each month
Departments argue over whose numbers are right
Decisions made on outdated data
Nobody notices a problem until it is expensive
faq: Which BI tool should we use?

Power BI is a strong default for Microsoft shops, Looker Studio suits Google-centric and budget-conscious teams, and Tableau excels at complex analysis. We recommend based on your data sources and users.
Do we need a data warehouse for dashboards?
Not always. Simple dashboards can connect directly to source systems. A warehouse becomes worthwhile when you combine many sources or need historical trends.
How do we make sure the numbers are right?
We document KPI definitions with your leadership, reconcile dashboard totals to source systems, and add data quality checks.

solutions.name: Data Warehouse & Pipeline Setup
solutions.tagline: One clean, historical home for all your business data, refreshed automatically.
solutions.text: A modern data stack that extracts data from your business systems, loads it into a cloud warehouse, and transforms it into clean, documented tables ready for reporting, analysis, and AI. Pipelines refresh on a schedule or in near real time, history is preserved even when source systems overwrite records, and data quality tests catch problems before they reach a dashboard. Your team gets a single source of truth that every report, model, and integration can rely on.
for: Companies combining data from five or more systems
Teams that need historical trend analysis
Businesses preparing data for AI and forecasting
features: Managed connectors for SaaS apps, databases, and files.
BigQuery, Snowflake, or Azure set up and secured.
Track how records change over time.
Alerts on missing, duplicate, or unexpected data.
Permissions and auditing for sensitive data.
problems: Analysts spend most of their time cleaning data
Historical data is lost when systems overwrite records
Every report pulls data a different way
AI projects stall on messy data
faq: What is a data warehouse?
A central database optimized for analysis that stores cleaned, combined data from your business systems, including history, so reporting and analytics run from one trusted source.
Is a data warehouse expensive to run?
For most small and midsize businesses, cloud warehouse costs are modest because you pay for storage and queries used. We design to keep costs predictable.
How often is the data refreshed?
Anywhere from daily to every few minutes, depending on how current the reports need to be and what the source systems allow.

solutions.name: Custom AI Agents & Assistants
solutions.tagline: AI that takes real actions in your systems, with guardrails and human approval where it matters.
solutions.text: Custom AI agents built to handle multi-step work that used to require a person: researching leads, triaging inboxes, drafting replies and proposals, updating records, answering staff questions from internal documents, and coordinating tasks across your tools. Each agent is connected to the systems it needs through secure, permissioned integrations, grounded in your data, and given clear limits, with human approval on actions that carry risk. Logs and evaluations show what each agent did and how well, so you can expand its responsibilities with confidence.
for: Teams buried in repetitive, judgment-light work
Businesses with knowledge spread across many documents
features: Find the tasks where an agent saves the most time safely.
Agents read and update your CRM, inbox, and apps through secure integrations.
Answers and actions based on your documents and data.
People approve sensitive actions before they happen.
Clear limits on what each agent can see and do.
Logs, quality checks, and cost tracking.
problems: Skilled staff spend hours on repetitive research and admin
Internal knowledge is hard to find
Off-the-shelf chatbots cannot take action
Concern about AI making unchecked mistakes
faq: What is an AI agent?
An AI agent is a system that uses a language model to plan and complete multi-step tasks, using tools like your CRM, email, or databases, rather than only answering questions in a chat window.
Is it safe to let AI update our systems?
With the right design, yes. Agents get only the permissions they need, risky actions require human approval, and every action is logged.
Will AI agents replace our staff?
In practice, agents remove repetitive work so people can focus on customers, judgment calls, and growth. Most clients redeploy time rather than reduce headcount.

solutions.name: AI Document Processing & Data Extraction
solutions.tagline: Turn invoices, forms, IDs, and PDFs into clean data in your systems, without typing.
solutions.text: An AI document processing pipeline that reads incoming documents (invoices, purchase orders, applications, intake forms, bills of lading, contracts, and scanned paperwork), extracts the fields you need, validates them against your rules and records, and posts the results into your ERP, CRM, or database. Documents arrive from email, upload portals, or scanners, low-confidence fields are sent to a quick human review queue, and every document is filed with its extracted data for audit.
for: Teams keying data from PDFs and paper forms
Logistics, insurance, healthcare, and finance operations
Businesses processing hundreds of documents a week
features: Email inboxes, portals, scanners, and shared drives.
Header fields, tables, and line items captured accurately.
Checks against vendors, customers, POs, and math.
Only uncertain fields need a person.
Data written to your ERP, CRM, or database automatically.
Every document stored with its extracted data.
problems: Staff retype data from PDFs all day
Typos cause billing and shipping errors
Paper backlogs build up at busy times
Hiring more people to keep up with volume
faq: How accurate is AI document extraction?
Accuracy is high on typed documents and improves with consistent layouts. Every field gets a confidence score, and anything below the threshold goes to a person, so errors are caught before posting.
Can it read handwriting?
Modern models handle clear handwriting reasonably well. For critical handwritten fields we route to human review.
What happens to our documents and data?
We use enterprise AI services with data protection terms, store documents in your environment where possible, and restrict access to those who need it.

solutions.name: Forecasting & Predictive Analytics
solutions.tagline: Predict demand, revenue, churn, and staffing needs so you can act before it happens.
solutions.text: Forecasting and predictive models built on your historical data to answer the questions that drive planning: how much will we sell, how much stock and staff will we need, which customers are likely to leave, and which leads are most likely to close. Models are trained and validated on your data, refreshed automatically, and delivered inside the tools your team already uses, such as reorder suggestions in your inventory system or churn-risk flags in your CRM, with plain-language explanations of what drives each prediction.
for: Service businesses planning staffing and capacity
features: Projections by product, location, and week.
At-risk customers flagged early for outreach.
Win likelihood based on your historical deals.
Labor needs matched to expected demand.
Predictions inside your CRM, ERP, or dashboards.
problems: Planning based on gut feel and last year's numbers
Overstock and stockouts at the same time
Customers leave without warning
Overstaffed slow days and understaffed busy ones
faq: How much data do we need for forecasting?
Generally at least one to two years of consistent history for seasonal forecasting. Simpler models can work with less, and we assess your data before committing to an approach.
How accurate will the forecasts be?
Accuracy depends on your data and how predictable your business is. We measure accuracy on held-out history and report it honestly before you rely on the model.
Do we need a data scientist to use the results?
No. Predictions are delivered as simple numbers, flags, and suggestions inside the tools your team already uses.
